title: SpikingLM: Towards Fully Spiking Language Model
claim: A full model is built from stacked blocks whose two novel components each work through a specific mechanism, enabling efficient inference.
layout: 4 panels: top architecture banner, three detail panels below, left-to-right
description: A wide figure with a top banner and three panels below it. The banner shows the SpikingLM Block repeated N times. Embeddings pass through spiking neurons into a Spike2Max Attention module and then a Spiking FFN. Each of Wq, Wk and Wv is followed by a green DAS box. The banner ends in an Output Head and a bar chart of next-token logits. A legend defines DAS, weight matrix, spiking neuron and matrix multiplication. The bottom-left panel, Distribution-aware Scaling, shows a membrane-potential histogram before and after scaling, with training and inference equations in the middle and spike trains underneath. The bottom-middle panel, Spike2Max, shows a diffuse attention map becoming a selective one through max-subtraction, bit-shift and winner-takes-all steps. The bottom-right panel contrasts training and inference, where DAS is fused into the weights and thresholds. Yellow, green and blue tints separate the parts.

abstract: Leveraging event-driven computation mechanism, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as a representative paradigm for energy-efficient edge intelligence. However, extending SNNs to modern deep language models still faces two fundamental challenges. First, dead neurons in deep SNNs lead to degraded gradients, limiting the training effectiveness of spiking language models. Second, removing Softmax for energy efficiency weakens token-wise competition, reducing the model’s ability to select salient tokens. To address these challenges, we propose Spiking Language Model (SpikingLM) to bridge the efficiency of SNNs and the capability of modern language models through two key innovations. First, we propose Distribution-aware Scaling method, which rescales linear outputs into an activation-friendly range to alleviate dead neurons and stabilize gradient propagation. Notably, its scaling parameters can be fused into the preceding linear layers, incurring no additional inference overhead. Second, we introduce Spike2Max to restore winner-takes-all mechanism via base-2 exponentiation and max-subtraction. Compared with Softmax, Spike2Max reduces energy consumption by over 95\% using hardware-efficient bit-shift operations. Experiments show that SpikingLM reduces energy consumption by 57.9\% and achieves state-of-the-art performance on GLUE, laying a promising foundation for energy-efficient language modeling. Code is available at~\url{https://github.com/hamings1/SpikingLM.git}.
